title: Descent of lisse condensed-coefficient modules across a surjective closed immersion
statement: Let $t:T\hookrightarrow W$ be a surjective closed immersion of schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-surjective-morphism], and let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring. Use the small pro-étale sites and internal modules over the pulled-back coefficient rings $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Let $M$ be a $\Lambda_W$-module and $t^*$ the actual coefficient-module inverse image [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback]. Then $M$ is lisse if and only if $t^*M$ is lisse, where lisse means locally finite free for a pro-étale covering, with rank zero allowed [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. More explicitly, given a pro-étale covering $\{C_a\to T\}$ and trivializations $(t^*M)|_{C_a}\cong\Lambda_{C_a}^{r_a}$, there are a pro-étale covering $\{B_b\to W\}$ and, for each $b$, an index $a(b)$ and a map $T_b=B_b\times_WT\to C_{a(b)}$ over $T$ such that $M|_{B_b}\cong\Lambda_{B_b}^{r_{a(b)}}$. The latter isomorphisms pull back along $t_b:T_b\to B_b$ to the prescribed pulled-back trivializations under the Cartesian coefficient identifications. No Noetherianity, reducedness, uniform rank, or bound on nilpotence is assumed.

proof.text: Suppose $M$ is lisse. Choose its covering $\{U_i\to W\}$ and finite-free isomorphisms as in the definition. The family $\{T\times_W U_i\to T\}$ is a cover: its arrows are weakly etale by base change, and it is fpqc by covering base change. Pull back each chosen isomorphism. The module composition isomorphisms identify its source with the restriction of $t^*M$ to $T\times_WU_i$; the maps $\kappa$ of step 1 identify its target with the same finite rank free coefficient module there. Thus $t^*M$ is lisse.

Apply Mathlib Functor.preimageIso to beta followed by the inverse of the canonical finite-free comparison kappa. The private abstract-functor lemma lift_compatible_iso proves F.map psi.hom followed by kappa.hom = beta.hom using Functor.map_preimage and the inverse identity of kappa. This is exactly the required equality with the prescribed trivialization.

proof.text: The covering $\{B_b\to W\}$ and the isomorphisms $u_b:M|_{B_b}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_{B_b}^{\oplus r_{a(b)}}$ satisfy the definition of lisse. Together with step 2 this proves both directions and the more explicit assertion. The proof selects a rank separately for each member, and never uses its uniqueness. Rank zero uses the empty biproduct in step 1. If $W$ is empty, its empty covering suffices; if the input family is empty then it covers only empty $T$, and surjectivity forces empty $W$. No Noetherian or nilpotence-bound assumption occurs in either of the two geometric tools.
